dedupe_keys.name: flood risk of a major hospital and a university centre built over a culverted stream in florence

description: This case study assesses flood risk for two critical facilities in Florence, Italy: one of the major hospitals of central Italy and a learning centre of the University of Florence, both built over a culverted stream within small sub-basins of the secondary river network. It is presented by Gabriele Bertoli and Chiara Arrighi in an abstract for the EGU General Assembly 2023 (15 May 2023), also listed in the University of Florence repository. The authors note that critical facilities are seldom included in flood risk analyses and that moving them away from main rivers can place them on poorly known minor streams with sudden responses. They ran a hydrological analysis and hydraulic modelling of the stream, supported by geophysical prospecting, derived a damage curve from building installations and systems, and assessed indirect impacts such as accessibility, disruption time, possible shelter use, occupancy changes and seasonality. Coverage: one hospital and one university centre in Florence. Access: open conference abstract. Licence: EGU abstracts are CC BY 4.0; free. Caveats: an abstract only, without numeric results. Simulation uses: flood impact functions for hospitals and schools. Related records: the USGS HERA community exposure data.
name: Flood risk of a major hospital and a university centre built over a culverted stream in Florence
organisations: University of Florence (Gabriele Bertoli, Chiara Arrighi)
outcomes: The study built a damage curve from building-specific installations and systems and a combined technique for direct and indirect impacts, including accessibility, service disruption time, shelter use, occupancy and seasonality.

Building-specific installations inventory and damage curve
